SourceString: A season of growth. Ingredients are easier to gather, and trade begins to stir after the winter's lull.
Long days favor business and labor, but the heat dries timber and thatch — fires spread more readily.
Rain soaks the city, slowing carts in the mud, yet the damp makes fires easier to contain.
Daylight is shortest, work grows harder, and sickness takes root in the cold.
Each season brings changes to daily life. Weather, daylight, and working hours vary with the season, shaping the rhythm of life in the city.
